description:
Measured 2026-09-14 on HEAD 95c3caa3a and on the pre-branch commit 4f49465f9 alike. A function whose parameter arrives as a lane-form tuple (transport ShapeDescr::Tuple, carrier Absent, one physical param per lane) and whose clause heads destructure it re-boxes that parameter on entry to run its dispatch: `lower_clause_dispatch_executable` (src/compiler2/jobs/native.rs:894) forces every dispatch-required input through `materialize_native_value`, which for a lane-form tuple emits `Prim::MakeTuple` -> `fz_alloc_struct`, then asks tuple_arity and reads the fields back off the heap. The interpreter does the same separately (src/ir_interp/backend.rs:702 select_clause, line 717). The clause helpers it tail-calls are clean; the whole cost is the entry.

Extern-free repro, identical on both commits: `defp pair(n), do: (if n > 0, do: {n, false}, else: {n, true}); defp unwrap({v, false}), do: v; defp unwrap({_, true}), do: -1` allocates one 32-byte struct per unwrap call. fz-5xp.30 did not introduce the defect; it routed every arithmetic operation through it (`arithmetic_result/1` has param_reprs [RawInt, RawAtom] and two entry params, and its entry re-boxes them), which is the whole of enum_list_allocations struct_allocs 0 -> 10, map_atom_order 3/96 -> 12/384, tree 3/144 -> 6/240.

The answer already exists one function away: ordinary body steps ask "field i of this bound value" through `transport_tuple_field` (native.rs:3885) and `transport_field_views` (native.rs:4037) without allocating. Entry dispatch asks the same question with an allocation. One question, two implementations.

Fix: entry dispatch becomes lane-aware. DispatchState carries NativeBoundValue instead of Var; `dispatch_subject_var` splits into a value form (TupleField on a Transport{Tuple} subject is lanes[i], emitting nothing) and a Var form used only where a single word is required; Region::TupleArity over a lane-form tuple is a compile-time constant, Region::Type over one is answered per field through transport_field_views; `lower_argument_bindings` takes bound values. The interpreter's select_clause takes the same shape, with the field-view calculator lifted to one shared place both doors call. Deleted as superseded: `delivered_tuple_fields`, `emit_delivered_tuple_test` and the `tuple_field_params` fast paths in native_codegen/prim.rs, and the `tuple_field_params` field that is never written (entry.rs, env.rs, function.rs). Not an inliner, not a macro, not an arithmetic table; fz-5xp.20 becomes an optimization rather than the remedy.

Proof, counts only: (1) the pair/unwrap program as a behavior fixture with heap counters, struct_allocs 0 on three doors, red at HEAD and at 4f49465f9; (2) a program-walk assertion through RequestedOutputSink that no dispatch-entry function contains Prim::MakeTuple (not a CLIF string match: the allocator renders as u0:N); (3) canon_test inventory width unchanged (lowering changed, identity did not); (4) goldens move only downward: enum_list_allocations {5,80,10,320,...} -> {5,80,0,0,...}, headline 400 -> 80; map_atom_order struct 12/384 -> 3/96; tree 6/240 -> 3/144. Docs: .agent/docs/pipeline.md (tuple-field transport), dispatch-matrix.md, pattern-matching.md; fixture headers of enum_list_allocations, tree, map_atom_order.
title: Entry dispatch re-boxes a lane-form tuple parameter to destructure it
